title: Best Day Trips from Kornati, Croatia 2027
metaDescription: Best day trips from Kornati: Telašćica, Krka, Šibenik, Zadar, Vransko Lake and Paklenica, with boat times, ticket prices in euros and local tips.
content:
## Where Day Trips from Kornati Start

Kornati National Park is an archipelago of 89 islands, islets and reefs with no bridge, no scheduled ferry and no permanent residents. Visitors arrive on boat tours or private boats. Overnight stays are limited to a few seasonal konobas and apartments in bays such as Vruje and Lavsa. Most people who want to explore beyond the archipelago base themselves in the mainland harbours of Murter, Betina, Biograd, Vodice or Šibenik, or in Zadar.

Plan trips from there. The national park itself is the main attraction, so the trips below cover places outside it, either by sea to neighbouring islands or by road along the Dalmatian coast.

## Telašćica Nature Park: The Easiest Sea Trip

Telašćica is a large bay on the southeast side of Dugi Otok, directly northwest of Kornati. The sea trip from Murter takes about 45–60 minutes. Many Kornati boat tours combine both parks in one day, which is the most efficient use of time.

### What to See

- **Telašćica Bay:** a long, sheltered natural harbour with several smaller bays. It is one of the safest anchorages in the Adriatic.
- **Cliffs on the open-sea side:** they drop about 160 m into the water, among the tallest in the Adriatic.
- **Lake Mir (Slano Jezero):** a salt lake about 1 km from the bay. It is warmer than the sea and popular for a short swim.

### Costs

Full-day group tours that include both Kornati and Telašćica generally cost about €35–65 per adult. Murter operators list the Kornati-only group trip at €65 per adult and €35 for children aged 5–12, with the park ticket, lunch and guide included. Children under 5 travel free on those trips. Boats usually leave Murter around 09:00.

Private speedboat charters for up to 11 guests start at roughly €950 per boat with the park ticket included. Shared small-boat tours out of Šibenik run about €120–150 per person.

The Kornati ticket is charged per boat, not per person. It is sold in advance at the shop on the park's website, in the mySea app and at the ABA reception in Murter. Buying from ranger boats inside the park costs noticeably more.

## Krka National Park: Waterfalls and Swimming Spots

Krka is the standard inland trip from the Murter and Šibenik coast. Drive about 1 hour from Murter to Skradin or Lozovac. The park has seven waterfalls along the Krka River, and Skradinski Buk is the largest and most photographed.

- **Entry:** about €20–40 per adult, with the highest price in peak summer and the lowest in winter. Children aged 7–18 pay about half, and younger children enter free.
- **Boat from Skradin:** the park boat to Skradinski Buk is included in the ticket in season.
- **Swimming:** swimming at Skradinski Buk was banned some years ago to protect the travertine. Check the current rule at the gate before packing swimwear.
- **Best time:** arrive at opening time or after 16:00. Midday coach groups from Split and Zadar fill the boardwalks.

Skip the Lozovac entrance in July and August if you can. Starting from Skradin means a calmer boat approach and a shorter wait, and the town has several konobas for a late lunch.

## Šibenik: A Stone Town Without Zadar's Crowds

Šibenik is about 30 km from Murter, a 35–45 minute drive. Its main sight is the Cathedral of St James, a UNESCO-listed Renaissance church built entirely of stone, with a frieze of 71 carved faces on the outer apse. Entry is about €5–10.

The town also has fortresses (St Michael's, St Nicholas at the harbour entrance, Barone and St John's). A combined ticket is about €10–15. The hill fortresses give the best views over the channel that leads to Kornati.

If you are only choosing one coastal town, Šibenik is the better value than Zadar. It is smaller, cheaper and less crowded, and it fits easily into a half day.

## Zadar and Sakarun Beach

Zadar is about 75 km from Murter, roughly 1 hour 15 minutes by car. Direct buses run from Murter and Šibenik, with fares of about €5–10 each way.

The sights worth the time are the Sea Organ, the Greeting to the Sun installation, the Roman Forum and the church of St Donatus. A standard walk through the peninsula takes 2–3 hours.

From Zadar, the ferry to Brbinj on Dugi Otok takes about 1 hour 30 minutes and costs about €8 per passenger. Sakarun Beach on the north end of the island is a white-pebble beach with clear shallow water. Speedboat tours from Zadar to Kornati sometimes add a Sakarun stop.

The Dugi Otok ferry looks like an easy day-trip add-on, but the timetable is tight. The last return sailing leaves early evening, and missing it means an overnight stay. Check the Jadrolinija timetable the day before and book a return seat in July and August.

## Vransko Lake Nature Park

Vransko Lake is Croatia's largest natural lake, about 40 km from Murter and 45 minutes by car. It is a bird-watching area with more than 250 recorded species. Cycling the lake's edges and the Kamenjak lookout are the main activities.

- **Entry:** about €5–10, with extra for bike rental.
- **Best time:** spring and autumn bird migration. In summer the heat is strong and there is little shade.
- **Viewpoint:** Kamenjak gives a view from the lake across to the Kornati archipelago on a clear day.

This trip suits families and travellers who want a slower day away from the water.

## Paklenica National Park: A Mountain Day

Paklenica sits below Velebit mountain, about 105 km from Murter and 1 hour 30 minutes by car. It has two canyons, Mala and Velika Paklenica, and is the main rock-climbing area in Croatia. Entry is about €10–15 in season.

The easy walk is the Velika Paklenica canyon path, about 3.5 km one way to the Paklenica mountain hut area, with a gentle climb. Longer routes to Vaganac or Anića Kuk need a full day and proper footwear.

Parking is limited at the main entrance in Starigrad-Paklenica. Arrive before 09:00 in July and August.

## Other Options Worth Knowing

- **Primošten:** a walled old town on a small peninsula, about 1 hour from Murter. It is known for the Babić wine region around the town.
- **Biograd na Moru:** a harbour town about 35 km from Murter with a long beach promenade. It also has a ferry link to Pašman and Ugljan.
- **Murter and Betina villages:** the shipbuilding heritage of Betina and the olive groves of Murter are both reachable on a short local drive.

## Which Day Trip Fits Which Traveller

| Traveller | Best choice |
|---|---|
| Short on time | Telašćica combined with Kornati boat tour |
| Families with children | Krka or Vransko Lake |
| History and architecture | Šibenik, then Zadar |
| Hikers and climbers | Paklenica |
| Beach focus | Sakarun Beach via Zadar |

## Practical Tips for Day Trips from Kornati

- **Check the weather first.** The bora and the strong jugo winds cancel boat tours. Murter operators state that trips depend on weather and passenger numbers, so keep the next day free as a backup.
- **Book park tickets ahead.** Kornati ticket prices rise sharply if you buy on site, and peak-season boat slots can sell out.
- **Rent a car for the mainland trips.** Public buses between Murter, Šibenik and Zadar run but are infrequent in the afternoon. A rental car makes combining Krka and Šibenik in a single day realistic.
- **Go early.** For Krka, Paklenica and Zadar, arrival before 09:00 avoids the heaviest crowds and heat.
- **Pack for sea and sun.** Boats offer little shade. Bring reef shoes for rocky swim stops, a hat and sunscreen.

## Best Time to Go

May, June and September have the best balance of warm sea and manageable crowds. July and August bring the highest prices, the busiest ferries and temperatures above 30°C. Many seasonal konobas in the archipelago close between October and April, and boat tours run less often.

faq.question: What are the best day trips from Kornati?
faq.answer: The best day trips are Telašćica Nature Park on Dugi Otok, Krka National Park, Šibenik, Zadar with Sakarun Beach, Vransko Lake and Paklenica. Telašćica is the easiest, since it is about 45–60 minutes by boat from Murter and often combined with Kornati tours.

faq.question: Where do you stay to do day trips from Kornati?
faq.answer: Most visitors stay in Murter, Betina, Biograd, Vodice, Šibenik or Zadar. The archipelago itself has only a few seasonal konobas and apartments, and no regular ferry or road connection.

faq.question: How much does a Kornati boat day trip cost?
faq.answer: Group tours cost about €35–65 per adult, and some Murter operators list €65 for adults and €35 for children aged 5–12, with the park ticket, lunch and guide included. Private speedboat charters for up to 11 guests start at about €950 per boat.

faq.question: Can you visit Krka National Park as a day trip from Murter?
faq.answer: Yes. Skradin is about 1 hour by car from Murter, and entry is about €20–40 depending on the season. Arrive early to avoid the midday coach groups.

faq.question: Is Telašćica worth visiting with Kornati?
faq.answer: Yes. Telašćica has a sheltered bay, cliffs about 160 m high and the salt lake Mir, and it is close enough to combine with Kornati in one full-day boat trip.

faq.question: What is the best time of year for day trips from Kornati?
faq.answer: May, June and September are best, with warm weather, calmer ferries and lower prices than July and August. Strong wind can cancel boat trips at any time, so keep a spare day in the plan.

faq.question: Do you need a car for day trips from Kornati?
faq.answer: A car is needed for Krka, Vransko Lake and Paklenica, because buses are infrequent. Boat trips to Telašćica and Zadar bus links work without one.

quickAnswer: The best day trips from Kornati are Telašćica Nature Park (about 1 hour by boat), Krka National Park and Šibenik (about 1.5 hours by road from Murter), Zadar and Sakarun Beach, Vransko Lake, and Paklenica. Most travellers base themselves in Murter, because Kornati has no hotels or regular ferries.
